messages.subject: Variance of encounter rates on recces
messages.subject_clean: Variance of encounter rates on recces
messages.body_plain:
Dear Group,

I'm using the R environment (with packages Distance and mrds) to analyse =
survey data of seven areas on multiple species and signs (dung, nests, =
vocalisation). These data also include travel recces. I used the =
jackknife method to estimate variances/standard errors of mean RAW =
encounter rates at recces (and at line transects). These estimates do =
marginally differ from those estimated with the "varn" function in mrds =
that implements methods of Fewster et al (2009). Note that survey is =
based on 30 transects/30 recces per area which may explain the small =
differences. The reason for using jackknife is that the "varn" function =
is defined internally and requires to extract the source code from the =
mrds package.

I have two main questions:

1] Can the variance methods of Fewster et al. be applied to recces, or =
is the Jackknife (or bootstrap) more appropriate (depending on sample =
size)? In the first case, it would be beneficial if the "varn" function =
can be accessed directly within R.

2] While R is a great environment to automate distance sampling e.g. =
evaluating detection functions, comparing raw encounter rates on recces =
with density/abundance on neighbouring transects etc., it requires =
programming skills. The Distance program is far more user-friendly (and =
has a great manual). Can Distance handle calculate raw encounter rates =
at recce data e.g. by assigning a fixed value for perpendicular =
distances?

with best regards,

Frank     =20

messages.subject: Re: Variance of encounter rates on recces
messages.subject_clean: Variance of encounter rates on recces
messages.body_plain:
Frank

You ask a computing question, but I think at the heart might be a
sampling issue.  Can you clarify your use of the term 'travel recces?'
I presume these are associated with your travel into locations where you
perform your random sampling, as mentioned in Section 7.8.5 of Buckland
et al. (2001).  I suspect you use tracks or trails for these recces.  If
that is the case, then the encounter rates (or their variances) are not
necessarily representative of the study area as your sampling scheme is
not randomly located (a necessity of design-based inference).

So it is possible to use the "varn" function in the mrds package
(hint--use the syntax "mrds:::varn(lvec, nvec, type)") but you must ask
yourself what that encounter rate and its variance is measuring.

messages.subject: Internal Error number: 457
messages.body_plain:
Hello List

Thank you in advance for any help you can give me.

I am working with passive acoustic detections of harbour porpoises during
line transect surveys.  I have managed to get abundance and density
estimates which seem accurate easily using CDS analysis without any errors.
I am now trying to use the DSM analysis to plot density changes over the
area we surveyed.  However I am having trouble with the MRDS engine.  It
won't run either half normal or hazard rate analysis due to Internal Error
457:

Initialising

Making data files

Making Data Selection Queries

**Error: Unexpected error **

Error Source: DataFileMaker.MakeObsQuery

Internal Error number: 457.

Internal Error description: "This key is already associated with an element
of this collection".

I haven't been able to find any other issues with this error on the site.  I
am using single observer data and have followed the dolphin sample project
closely in hopes to avoid errors.  I have re-loaded my data and checked it
several times to make sure nothing is listed twice or shares the same Label.
If anyone has any guidance on this it would be much appreciated.

Many thanks

Anna

Anna Cucknell

MCR International

Hello,

I'm attempting to use the DSM engine (Distance 6.0 Release 2) to create a=
 density surface model of the counts of observations within segements of =
line transects. I've succesfully estimated a detection function for my da=
ta using the MRDS engine and I'm attempting to use the detection probabil=
ities from that detection function in my density surface model.

When running the analysis I get the following error message:

Initializing=20
Making data files=20
Making Data Selection Queries=20
The following fields will be written to the data file, and can be used in=
 model formulae. Note that you should use the new names, not the original=
 field names in formulae, and that formulae names are case sensitive.
  Format: [layer name].[field name] AS new name
  [Segment].[Label] AS label
  [Segment].[Line length] AS line.length
  [Segment].[NDVI] AS ndvi
  [Segment].[TRI] AS tri
  [Segment].[Marine] AS marine
  [Segment].[PW] AS pw
  [Sample].[Label] AS sample.label
  [Sample].[Line length] AS sample.line.length
  [Sample].[TimeCode] AS timecode
  [Sample].[Year] AS year
  [Region].[Label] AS stratum.label
  [Region].[Area] AS area
  [Study area].[Label] AS global.label
=20
** Error: Encountered a problem while executing the data creating query '=
qry2_DsmSample.  **

I've seen multiple posts about this error, but none seem to offer a solut=
ion. There is a bug reported on bugzilla that  is suggested to be the cau=
se of this problem:

Bug 85-=20
Single platform data error: =E2=80=9C** Error: Encountered a problem whil=
e executing the data creating query 'qry[x]_DsmSample. **=E2=80=9D

Bugzilla also suggests this bug was fixed in September 2010, but I'm usin=
g the latest version of Distance and I'm still getting this error message=
.

One list member mentioned that they encountered this problem because one =
of their layer names was the same as a field name and that once they chan=
ged this, the problem was solved:

https://www.jiscmail.ac.uk/cgi-bin/webadmin?A2=3Dind1010&L=3Ddistance-sam=
pling&P=3DR2&1=3Ddistance-sampling&9=3DA&J=3Don&d=3DNo+Match%3BMatch%3BMa=
tches&z=3D4

I've inspected all of my field and layer names and I do not have any that=
 are the same.

Does anyone know of a solution for this error?

Thanks for your time,
Barry Robinson

messages.subject: Solutions to: Internal Error 457, Error 91 and Error about effort
messages.subject_clean: Solutions to: Internal Error 457, Error 91 and Error about effort
messages.body_plain:
Hello list

Thanks to the very patient Eric Rexstad, several errors and problems I had
with the MRDS and DSM engines were corrected.  I have provided a summary
below in order to help anyone who has any of these issues in the future.  As
a little background I was working with passive acoustic detections from a
line transect based survey (single observer).

Problem 1: Internal Error 457: "This key is already associated with an
element of this collection"

I managed to get abundance and density estimates which seem accurate easily
using CDS analysis without any errors. However when trying to the MRDS
engine it wouldn't run either half normal or hazard rate analysis due to
Internal Error 457.

Solution:  The MDRS engine wants to work with double observer data, and even
though you can trick it into using single observer data the settings for the
survey type must be set to double observer and have a field 'Observer' which
would contain '1' for all detections.

Problem 2:  **Error: The layer 'Line transect' specified by the Survey for
calculating efforts is higher than the sample layer specified in the Model
Definition.
Correct effort values can therefore not be calculated.**

Solution: Change the survey properties.  Visit the Surveys Tab, Properties
button, Data fields tab and change the Effort Role to which ever layer
contains the Effort (for me the Segment layer).

If you look at the Dolphin.dst example, the effort is to be defined at the
segment (subsample1) layer of your project with a field found there.  This
is different to the way in which "normal" distance sampling works wherein we
are interested in the lengths of various segments.  With DSM, the modelling
is taking place at the level of the transect segments, so Distance needs to
know the size of the segments (defined using the field called 'Effort') that
contains the length of each segment.

Problem 3: Error 91: **Error Unexpected error** "Object variable or With
block variable not set". - in the DSM analysis

Solution: The problem was as simple as rerunning the detection function
fitting analyses after you had changed the Analysis preferences such that
the objects were not erased after their creation.  I suspect you had run
analysis 1, then reset the preferences such that analysis 1 R results were
retained, then run your dsm analysis that complained that the analysis 1
results could not be found.

I hope this helps anyone having a simlar issues and thanks again to Eric
Rexstad from St Andrews University for his patientce and help with these
issues.

Anna

Anna Cucknell

Marine Conservation Research Ltd.

Marine Conservation Research International
